column1: # Recording script for the first STT comparison (step 2.1.g): 50 items.
# Columns (tab separated): id, how to say it, what to say (read aloud as written), expected digits.
#  - One file per item, WAV or m4a, named <id>_<speaker>_<condition>.wav  (e.g. C06_igor_car.wav).
#    Say only the text; keep ~0.5 s of silence before and after; do not read the id or the style.
#  - Conditions: quiet = quiet room; car = in the car (engine on, windows closed), phone on the
#    dashboard or handsfree/Bluetooth as a customer would; street = outside.
#  - Suggested split: you record all 50 in a quiet room, then A01-A05, C01-C10, D01-D04, E01-E06 in
#    the car. Each friend records the C and E items (16) plus 8-10 of A, B, D in mixed conditions.
#  - Record with the phone's voice memo (wideband). The telephone channel (8 kHz, G.711) is
#    simulated afterwards, so record normally, not over a call.
#  - The numbers in C01-C10 are invented; read them as written. C06-C08 are dictated IN PIECES with
#    a pause at every comma: they test whether the recogniser cuts the number off at a pause.
#  - S01/S02 contain no speech: they test for text invented out of silence and noise.
# Only record yourself and people who agreed to it. Recordings go to data/stt_eval/ (git-ignored).
